title: 30-minute instrumented SDK bootcamp outline (scratch)
content:
Goal: a tight 30-minute hands-on SDK bootcamp that gets a developer from zero to an instrumented hello-world that reports latency, token counts, and failure modes to Redwood Console. Focus is on low-friction, reproducible steps and patterns developers can copy into production apps.

Audience: engineers who have used an HTTP API but are new to Redwood SDKs and to basic LLM observability practices. Not for deep ML folks — pragmatic, engineering-first.

Constraints / guardrails:
- Must complete within 30 minutes on a laptop (mac/linux) with wifi.
- Minimal prerequisites: git, node 18+ or python 3.10+, Redwood API key.
- All steps runnable offline against a local sandbox stub (we provide a small stub server / docker image).
- Keep third-party deps to a minimum; prefer Redwood client + tiny telemetry helper.

Quick flow (30-min timeline):
- 0:00–02:00 — Welcome + context (what we ship, why instrument)
  - Two slides: one showing cost/latency tradeoffs and one showing how observability prevents regressions.
- 02:00–06:00 — Setup (git clone, install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, start local stub)
  - Provide exact commands for mac/linux and quick failure troubleshooting snippet.
- 06:00–12:00 — Hello world: call text generation & streaming example
  - Show JS and Python minimal examples. Emphasize streaming vs non-streaming paths.
  - Hands-on: run the example and inspect output.
- 12:00–18:00 — Add lightweight instrumentation
  - Add SDK middleware wrapper that logs: request_id, model, prompt_length, response_tokens, latency_ms, status_code, error_message.
  - Send telemetry to local sink and to Redwood Console demo workspace (toggle via env var).
- 18:00–25:00 — Failure and fallback patterns
  - Simulate throttling, model fallback, and network blips.
  - Validate the app picks up fallback policy and emits expected metrics & traces.
- 25:00–29:00 — Quick polish: a simple test and one pager summary
  - Run smoke test that asserts 200s for nominal flow, and proper metric names for failure cases.
- 29:00–30:00 — Q&A + next steps checklist

Files we ship for the workshop (repo layout):
- /examples/bootcamp/README.md (one-liner + run commands)
- /examples/bootcamp/js/hello_instrumented.js (minimal SDK + middleware)
- /examples/bootcamp/py/hello_instrumented.py (same in python)
- /examples/bootcamp/stub/README + dockerfile (small stub that simulates delays/errors)
- /examples/bootcamp/tests/smoke_test.sh
- /docs/bootcamp-telemetry-patterns.md (reference patterns + event schema)

Instrumentation patterns (keep it tiny, copyable):
1) Request wrapper: capture start_ts, end_ts, compute latency_ms, count prompt tokens and response tokens (best-effort).
2) Normalize event names: "redwood.request.start", "redwood.request.complete", "redwood.request.error".
3) Tag set: {team, route, model, model_size_estimate, region, installed_version, env}. Keep tags shallow.
4) Use sampling for verbose traces (>1s) to avoid cost blowup. Always sample errors.
5) Expose a local /metrics endpoint for prometheus-compatible scraping for quick local dashboards.

Minimal event schema (single-line examples kept tiny for quick copy):
- redwood.request.complete | request_id | latency_ms | prompt_tokens | response_tokens | status=200 | model=gptx-zi | env=dev
- redwood.request.error | request_id | latency_ms | error_type | http_code | model | env

Lab exercises / checkpoints (for instructors):
- Checkpoint 1 (after 12min): participant can run hello and see the model response.
- Checkpoint 2 (after 18min): participant pushes a metric to the local sink and can see event in local dashboard.
- Checkpoint 3 (after 25min): participant triggers fallback and verifies fallback counter increments.

Cheatsheet: quick commands
- git clone ... && cd examples/bootcamp
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...
- npm i && node js/hello_instrumented.js OR python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r py/requirements.txt && python py/hello_instrumented.py
- docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 redwood/bootcamp-stub:latest (if using stub)

Common failure modes & triage notes (notes-to-self):
- "can't reach stub" -> check docker mapped port, firewall (mac: allow incoming).
- "streaming not working" -> confirm node version > 18 + enable SSE polyfill for older browsers.
- "no telemetry in console" -> check REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_TARGET env var, ensure sample rate not zero.
- "token counts off" -> tokenization mismatch; document the tokenizer used by stub (gpt2-like) and include helper util.

Open questions to resolve before next run:
- Should we include the advanced KV-cache demo? that's >10 min, probably for v2.
- What default sampling rate should we ship in example? 0.02 or 0.05? Ask Observability team (ticket linked).
- Should instructor slide deck include cost-per-1M-tokens quick table? good idea, get numbers from Finance.

TODOs (backlog):
- [ ] Finalize smoke_test.sh and make CI job that runs on PRs to examples/bootcamp.
- [ ] Add one-click Cloud Playground button for demo workspace.
- [ ] Update docs/bootcamp-telemetry-patterns with concrete code snippets for Java, Go.
- [ ] Run a pilot internally with Solutions Eng and record time-to-complete metrics.

Instructor notes: keep pace brisk, aim for people to copy/paste not to understand every kernel. Encourage copy of instrumentation into their app repo; emphasize small wins (latency + fallback counters) over full tracing.

Reference links inside content: Linear ticket (see linked_artifacts), demo PR for middleware example (github link above).

Quick sign-off checklist before sharing externally:
- code linted and minimal deps (satisfy security scan)
- stub contains no proprietary prompts or customer data
- example uses a non-production API key sandbox OR clearly uses env var and warns participants

Notes to self end — keep this as a living scratch doc. If time, convert to a polished "bootcamp recipe" doc and add to developer-onboarding playbooks folder.
